newsitem.title: USA: FDA to ease regulation of home drug test kits.
newsitem.headline: FDA to ease regulation of home drug test kits.

text.p: The Food and Drug Administration, responding to congressional criticism, said Thursday it would ease its regulation of home kits that allow parents to test their children for drug use.

"Because there is value in having drugs of abuse test systems available for use in the home setting, we believe that it should be easier to get them onto the market for such use," FDA Deputy Commissioner William Schultz said at a House Commerce subcommittee hearing.
Subcommittee members had criticised FDA regulation of home drug test kits as too stringent at a hearing last September.
The kits usually have a container for collecting urine samples and packaging for mailing the sample to a laboratory.

Schultz said after reviewing its policies, the FDA had decided to let companies market home drug test kits without prior agency approval if the test used has been recognised as safe and reliable, if the laboratory doing the testing has been certified and if samples are adequately identified.

"Because there are more than 200 FDA-cleared urine tests for detecting drugs of abuse and hundreds of federally certified laboratories capable of conducting this testing, accurate and reliable testing is available now," Schultz said.
He said concerns expressed by some FDA employees that home drug tests might cause problems between parents and children were misplaced.

"Concerns about the effect of a product on the parent-child relationship or family discord have no place in the agency's determination as to whether that product meets the requirements of the Federal Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act," he said.
Schultz said the FDA hoped to issue a rule on home drug test kits in about two years after public hearings and comment.
"In the meantime, the agency will not actively regulate drugs of abuse test systems used in the workplace, insurance or sports settings," he said.
